name: Barbell Back Squat
summary: A foundational lower-body lift that loads the quads, glutes and trunk through a full squat pattern. It builds leg strength and muscle and carries over to most other leg work.
setup: Set the bar in a rack at about upper-chest height and step under it so it rests across your upper back (on the rear delts for a low bar, on the traps for a high bar).
Grip the bar just outside your shoulders, pull your shoulder blades together and unrack it with a straight back.
Take two or three small steps back and set your feet about shoulder width with toes turned out slightly.
Take a big breath into your belly and brace your trunk before each rep.
execution: Start the descent by pushing your hips back and bending your knees together, keeping your whole foot on the floor.
Keep your chest up and your knees tracking in line with your toes as you lower to at least thigh parallel, or as deep as you can control with a neutral spine.
Pause briefly at the bottom without relaxing your brace.
Drive through the whole foot and stand up, keeping your hips and chest rising at the same rate.
Exhale at the top, re-brace and repeat; re-rack by walking forward until the bar touches the hooks.
mistakes: Knees caving inward: think about spreading the floor apart with your feet and push the knees out in line with the toes.
Heels lifting or weight shifting to the toes: keep pressure through the midfoot and heel and widen the stance or lower the weight if needed.
Hips shooting up first so the torso folds forward: slow the ascent, keep the chest up and reduce the load.
Cutting depth short with heavy weight: use a load you can take to a consistent depth, ideally set safety pins in the rack.
